text:
Alex: FYI AuditBot just flagged the new EU retention policy rollout — default retention increased to 5y for flowlogs and keystore auditlines.
AuditBot: policy_update: EU-AUDIT-RETENTION=5y applied to prod-eu. Affects: flowlogs, keystore, natgw-logs.
Maria: ugh that will blow up our natgw egress volume and S3 cost. Any immediate numbers?
Devon: rough calc: +3.2TB/day of logs per region if we keep full fidelity for all nodes. Monthly ~90TB, cost delta ~€18k/mo before transfer/storage optimization.
Samir: Also: provisioning side-effect — keystore calls spike during node boot (decrypts + attestation). With audit retention we keep more meta which increases verification cost for historical lookups.
Lee: we've already seen higher conntrack on eu warm pools. Yesterday ~15% slower joins when flowlog write QPS spiked.
Alex: Right. Prod-eu GPU onboarding latency went from 70s -> 130s in two waves. Ops correlated to NAT egress saturation (SRE-bot logs).
SRE-bot: alert: natgw-egress-queue > 85% for prod-eu-az1  (1712923500).
FinanceOps: if numbers hold that €18k, we need to propose a mitigation plan to limit Q2 overruns. Paging eng-platform and security for options.
Maria: immediate mitigations we can deploy: 1) sample flowlogs (10%) 2) TTL-based retention for debug-level logs 3) export aggregated metrics instead of raw logs for warm-pool nodes.
Devon: +1 sampling. Also consider moving full-fidelity audit to cold storage (Glacier-equivalent) and store only pointers in hot S3 to reduce hot egress.
Samir: Security note: can't drop keystore audit fidelity for service accounts used by customers (reg requirement). We can sample infra-level keystore logs but need to keep complete trail for customer-signed actions.
Lee: operational hack: add a staging fallback region (prod-eu-lite) with relaxed audit for onboarding bursts. Would let us keep SLA for joins while full-eu throughput stabilizes. But regulatory team might not accept.
Alex: @FinanceOps can we cost-share reserve dedicated natgw throughput for the onboarding window? That avoids tail latency while we iterate.
FinanceOps: possible but needs SRE justification. Need <= €10k/month commitment to sign off quickly.
Maria: long-term: move keystore attestation cache to local LRU per node (reduce calls to central keystore during warmup). Small change, big impact on boot QPS.
Devon: prototype snippet for local cache in node-agent: 
```
cache.get(key) || (resp = keystore.decrypt(key); cache.set(key, resp, ttl=24h))
```
Samir: assume tamper-evidence retained? We need to sign cached attestations with transient keys to keep audit integrity.
Alex: ok plan proposal: 1) roll sampling to 10% for infra flowlogs (deploy today) 2) enable node-agent local keystore cache + signed attestations (devon + samir) 3) finance to approve short-term natgw burst reserve if cost delta > threshold 4) run 72h canary in prod-eu-lite for onboarding behavior.
Lee: timeline?
Devon: can do sampling toggle in 2 hours, cache PR in 2 days, canary in 3 days.
FinanceOps: provisional approval for €8k/month burst reserve pending SRE postmortem after canary.
Samir: I'll stub the signing workflow and security review request now.
AuditBot: audit_ticket created: #EU-AUD-4477 (retention mitigation trace).
Alex: thanks. If anyone sees join failures spike after sampling toggle revert immediately and ping #oncall.
Maria: noted. I'll post a short runbook for the sampling rollback and cost tracking dashboard.
Lee: I'll schedule a 30m sync after canary start to review metrics (join latency, natgw QPS, keystore QPS).
SRE-bot: scheduled: canary-run prod-eu-lite start=1713000000 duration=72h.
Alex: good thread. Keep updates concise here. :thumbsup:
